requirement: Every CORE item's tests pass against Postgres, and each new operation is in openapi.json, on /mcp, and refused without its scope.

A service call on every CORE-30 operation leaves out a walled matter's records and answers not_found on a walled get; lifting the wall returns them on the next read. The one exception is the occupancy read, which also returns the events of walled matters with no assigned attendee user as start and end intervals only (Patrick's 2026-11-21 ruling, section 1); from core update 2i an attendee counts as assigned only while active, and each occupancy interval also carries all_day (Patrick's 2026-11-24 approval, section 1).
A contract call reaches only a provider the admin linked; unlinking stops it at once with contract_unlinked; neither module ever receives the other's address.
A public page serves with no session, refuses an operation not in public_operations, and answers 429 past the rate setting.
Every row CORE-36 names is closed in CONTRIBUTOR-GAPS.md, each with a test that failed before the fix.
After the billing move, every invoice, payment and expense reads the same through the API as before, to the cent, and a module foreign key to core.invoices installs and holds.
matter-clock and the five batch 1 modules install, run and uninstall on the updated core with no change to their packages.
The update applies overnight with no failed requests during the core's update load test, and a fresh install reaches first-run setup with no module installed.
The form makes a sent invoice with one "Balance forward as of" line, its historical number and imported true; the next normal invoice takes the next number in the sequence, unchanged.
A number at or above invoice_number_start, a duplicate number, an amount of zero or less, or a missing matter is refused with a message naming the reason, and nothing is written.
A CSV of 500 rows with one bad row writes nothing and the preview names the bad row; with the row fixed, all 500 land in one transaction.
Re-running the same CSV writes nothing new and reports every row as already imported by external_ref.
Amount paid to date posts one imported payment and the balance due equals amount due less amount paid.
The client sees the document of record in the portal for an imported invoice, and staff open it from the billing tab.
Voiding an imported invoice works and logs the void; the sequence is untouched.
The collections panel, aging and statements include imported invoices exactly like others.
A package with a structured price lists that price as the provider's information, with the "Sold and licensed by" line; a package with the old string still lists.
Uploading the kit's signed file unchanged succeeds; a tampered one is refused.
The author changes the listed price and sales link without a new package; the listing shows both at once, and nothing is charged, sent or changed on any install.
A priced module installs from the local marketplace with no key and no payment step.
The marketplace has no checkout, subscription, renewal, refund, payment-service connection, platform fee or price-change notice: no route, setting, state record, email or dependency for any of them.
No payment detail, license key or provider secret appears in marketplace state, logs or responses.
No marketplace test or code path reaches a payment service or any outside host; test helpers refuse any other host.
